title: Calculateur de risque ASCVD 2013 (maladie cardiovasculaire athéroscléreuse) de l’AHA/ACC
formula: Les informations relatives au calcul du score sont disponibles dans l'[annexe 7 de l'étude de Goff, et al. 2014](https://circ.ahajournals.org/content/circulationaha/129/25_suppl_2/S49.full.pdf).

how_to_use.why:
- Identifie les patients appartenant à des groupes à risque plus élevé, susceptibles d’avoir un bénéfice net plus important et un nombre de sujets à traiter plus faible pour un traitement par statine et un traitement antihypertenseur.
- Permet une décision médicale partagée entre cliniciens et patients.
- Adapte l’intensité des traitements prévent
how_to_use.when:
- Appliquer chez les adultes asymptomatiques âgés de 40–75 ans avec un LDL-C de 70–189 mg/dL sans ASCVD connue, lorsqu'on envisage des interventions de prévention primaire, en particulier un traitement par statine.
- Ne pas utiliser chez :

 - Adultes <40 ou >75 ans (données limitées sur la performance).
 - Patients avec ASCVD connue.
 - Adultes avec un LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL, y compris l'hypercholestérolémie familiale (un traitement hypolipémiant est indiqué indépendamment du risque calculé).
how_to_use.pearls:
**Pearls:**

- Well calibrated near clinical decision thresholds (7.5%-10% risk) in broad U.S. populations.
- First risk calculator to provide sex- and race-specific estimates and include stroke as an outcome.
- Extensively validated in multiple external cohorts.
- Best validated in non-Hispanic White and non-Hispanic Black adults in the United States.

**Pitfalls:**

- Derived from cohorts recruited between the 1940s and 1980s, potentially overestimating risk in contemporary populations receiving modern preventive therapies.
- Performance is highly variable in non-U.S. populations.
- Less accurate in patients already receiving intensive preventive interventions.
- May overestimate risk in:

 - Patients with higher socioeconomic status or receiving consistent preventive care.
 - Patients with predicted 10-year risk >10%.
- May underestimate risk in:

 - Asian and Hispanic adults, who were underrepresented in derivation cohorts.
 - Patients with lower socioeconomic status.
 - Chronic inflammatory conditions (e.g., HIV, rheumatoid arthritis, sarcoidosis, psoriasis).
 - Familial hypercholesterolemia.

next_steps.advice:
Interpret results of this tool within the clinical context, and consider the following during the clinician-patient discussion:

- Absolute risk estimate.
- Net benefit of therapy.
- Socioeconomic status.
- Patient preferences and values.
- Risk-enhancing factors, including:

 - Family history of premature ASCVD.
 - Persistently elevated LDL-C ≥160 mg/dL.
 - Metabolic syndrome.
 - Chronic kidney disease.
 - History of preeclampsia or premature menopause (age <40 years).
 - Chronic inflammatory disorders (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, HIV).
 - High-risk ethnicity (e.g., South Asian ancestry).
 - Persistent triglyceride elevation ≥175 mg/dL.
- Supporting studies, when available:

 - Apolipoprotein B ≥130 mg/dL.
 - hs-CRP ≥2.0 mg/L.
 - Ankle-brachial index (ABI) <0.9.
 - Lipoprotein(a) ≥50 mg/dL.
next_steps.management:
Treatment thresholds based on this tool are historical, as ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guidelines now recommend [PREVENT](nabda:calc.predicting-risk-cardiovascular-disease-events-prevent) for primary prevention risk assessment; if this tool is used, the following management thresholds might be considered:

- **10-year ASCVD risk ≥7.5%:** Consider initiating moderate- or high-intensity statin therapy after clinician-patient discussion.

 - If 10-year risk ≥20%: Consider high-intensity statin to reduce LDL-C ≥50%.
 - If 10-year risk 7.5%–19.9%: Consider moderate-intensity statin to reduce LDL-C ≥30%.
- **10-year ASCVD risk 5% to <7.5%:**

 - Evaluate risk-enhancing factors.
 - Consider statin therapy if risk enhancers present.
 - May use coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring to refine the treatment decision.
- **10-year ASCVD risk <5%:**

 - Emphasize lifestyle modification.
 - Reassess risk factors every 4–6 years.
- **For stage 1 hypertension** (130–139/80–89 mm Hg): Categorize as <10% or ≥10% 10-year ASCVD risk for therapeutic decisions, and refer to most recent AHA/ACC guidelines.
- **Follow-up:**

 - Reassess lipids 4–12 weeks after statin initiation or dose adjustment.
 - Repeat every 3–12 months as needed.
 - Assess adherence and percentage LDL-C reduction from baseline.

short_description: Risque de maladie cardiaque ou d’AVC à 10 ans.
medium_description: Determine 10-year risque de hard ASCVD, i.e. infarctus du myocarde, AVC, ou death due pour coronary heart maladie ou AVC.

before_use:
This calculator includes inputs based on race. See the[Quality Rating rationale](#evidence)for more information.

- Learn more about[our approach](https://www.mdcalc.com/race)to addressing race and bias on MDCalc.
- Looking for a race-free equation to calculate CVD risk? Check out the [PREVENT](nabda:calc.predicting-risk-cardiovascular-disease-events-prevent) score.

As of 2026, the ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guidelines recommends using [PREVENT](nabda:calc.predicting-risk-cardiovascular-disease-events-prevent) over this tool for primary prevention risk assessment because of improved accuracy, more contemporary derivation cohorts, and elimination of race-based estimation. [PREVENT](nabda:calc.predicting-risk-cardiovascular-disease-events-prevent) provides risk estimates approximately 40%–50% lower than the 2013 ASCVD Risk Score for the same risk factor profile, with correspondingly adjusted treatment thresholds (≥3% for PREVENT vs ≥5% for the 2013 ASCVD Risk Score).
instructions:
- Notre [algorithme de risque d’ASCVD](nabda:calc.ascvd-atherosclerotic-cardiovascular-disease-risk-algorithm-including-known-ascvd-aha-acc) est une approche par étapes pour tous les patients adultes – y compris ceux ayant une ASCVD connue.
- Ce calculateur ne doit être utilisé que chez les patients adultes sans ASCVD connue et avec un LDL 70-189 mg/dL (1.81-4.90 mmol/L).
